title: Tiny $70 Xteink X3 e-reader
summary:
The article reviews the Tiny $70 Xteink X3 e-reader, a credit card-sized, magnetic device designed to attach to an iPhone. Despite its appearance as a cheap gimmick with a "plasticky" build, basic hardware (no touchscreen, color, or backlight), and poor preloaded software, the author hails it as the single best piece of technology purchased in years.

The X3's small size is its key strength, making it convenient to carry everywhere and encouraging more reading. The author's reading output increased significantly, and phone screen time decreased. Its "TikTokification of reading"—breaking books into short paragraphs per page—creates an addictive experience that serves as a healthy alternative to doomscrolling.

Despite its flaws, the Xteink X3 has become a viral hit, with users creating custom accessories and developing open-source firmware like Crosspoint, which significantly upgrades the device with features like custom fonts, reading stats, and Libby integration. The author argues that the Xteink represents a crucial trend: cheap, simple, and customizable gadgets, often from China, are filling a gap left by predictable, expensive "innovations" from Silicon Valley, bringing much-needed fun back to consumer electronics.
chinese_title: 70美元迷你Xteink X3电纸书
chinese_summary:
本文评测了售价70美元的微型Xteink X3电子阅读器，这是一款信用卡大小的磁吸设备，旨在吸附到iPhone上。尽管它看起来像一个廉价的小玩意儿，具有塑料感十足的结构、基础硬件（无触摸屏、彩色显示或背光）以及糟糕的预装软件，作者却将其誉为多年来购入的最佳科技产品。

X3的小巧尺寸是其关键优势，使其方便随身携带，并鼓励人们阅读更多。作者的阅读量显著增加，手机屏幕使用时间减少。它的“阅读TikTok化”——将书籍内容按页分解为短段落——创造了一种令人上瘾的体验，成为了替代“刷屏焦虑”（doomscrolling）的健康选择。

尽管有其不足，Xteink X3已成为一款爆款产品，用户纷纷为其制作定制配件，并开发了Crosspoint等开源固件，这极大地升级了设备，带来了自定义字体、阅读统计和Libby集成等功能。作者认为，Xteink代表了一个重要的趋势：廉价、简单且可定制的小工具，通常来自中国，正在填补硅谷那些可预测、昂贵的“创新”所留下的空白，将消费者电子产品急需的乐趣带了回来。

title: Programming is Art
summary:
The author initially found programming to be an art, consumed by the ability to create new programs from scratch, learning various technologies, and developing a unique coding style. Their early motivation was the sheer fascination of building things. However, over time, their interest shifted; while they still enjoyed the creative process of building startups, the act of writing code became a means to an end—primarily for financial gain. They preferred managerial roles and delegating coding tasks, focusing on product creation rather than the coding itself.

This perspective contrasts sharply with "true programmers" whom the author describes as artists. These individuals are driven by an intrinsic passion for coding, enjoying problem-solving, design, logic, and understanding systems, regardless of income. They might work on open-source projects for no financial reward, valuing the process itself.

This distinction underpins their differing views on AI. While the author uses AI for efficiency in building projects for profit, they acknowledge that AI's benefits are irrelevant to these "artist" programmers. For artists, the claim that AI will replace them is illogical because their desire to code is an unyielding, intrinsic drive that no technological breakthrough can diminish.

The author concludes by likening this to their own writing process: they avoid AI for writing, valuing the personal thought, emotion, and creative process over soulless, AI-generated text. For them, writing is an art pursued independently of money, a sentiment they believe true programmers share for coding.
chinese_title: 编程是艺术
chinese_summary:
作者起初视编程为一门艺术，沉醉于从零开始创建新程序、学习各种技术、并发展出独特的编码风格。他们早期的动力源于对创造事物的纯粹着迷。然而，随着时间的推移，他们的兴趣发生了转变；尽管他们仍然享受创建初创公司的创造过程，但写代码本身变成了达到目的的手段——主要是为了经济利益。他们更喜欢管理角色，将编码任务委派出去，专注于产品创造，而非编码本身。

这种观点与作者所描述的“真正的程序员”（即艺术家）形成了鲜明对比。这些人是受内在的编程热情所驱动的，无论收入如何，他们都享受解决问题、设计、逻辑和理解系统的乐趣。他们甚至可能会无偿地参与开源项目，重视过程本身。

这种区别是他们对人工智能看法差异的基础。尽管作者利用人工智能提高盈利性项目构建的效率，但他们承认人工智能的好处与这些“艺术家”程序员无关。对艺术家而言，声称人工智能会取代他们是不合逻辑的，因为他们对编码的渴望是一种坚不可摧的内在驱动力，任何技术突破都无法削弱。

作者最后将此比作他们自己的写作过程：他们避免使用人工智能写作，重视个人的思想、情感和创作过程，而非毫无灵魂的人工智能生成文本。对他们而言，写作是一种独立于金钱的艺术追求，他们相信真正的程序员对编码也抱有同样的情感。

title: Live map of public transport in Belgium
summary: "ovlive" is a live, real-time map showcasing public transport across Belgium. It consolidates information from all major Belgian transport operators—De Lijn, STIB-MIVB, TEC, and NMBS—onto a single interactive map. Users can view every bus, tram, metro, and train in real-time, complete with up-to-date delay information, designated stops, and departure times. The service aims to provide a comprehensive, unified overview of public transport movement throughout the country.
chinese_title: 比利时公共交通实时地图
chinese_summary: "ovlive" 是一个展示比利时全境公共交通的实时地图。它整合了比利时所有主要交通运营商——De Lijn、STIB-MIVB、TEC 和 NMBS——的信息，并将其呈现在一张交互式地图上。用户可以实时查看每一辆巴士、有轨电车、地铁和火车，并附带最新的延误信息、指定停靠站和发车时间。该服务旨在提供全国公共交通动态的全面统一概览。

title: AI, Tools and Transformation
summary:
The article "AI, Tools and Transformation" challenges the optimistic view that AI will effortlessly automate corporate tasks and simplify software development. It notes that companies, despite vast software estates, remain burdened by repetitive work. While AI promises easy tool creation without coding, the author argues this overlooks fundamental realities.

Firstly, most individuals aren't "tool-builders" and don't instinctively identify automation opportunities. The core difficulty isn't building tools, but knowing *what* problem needs a tool and *what* that tool should accomplish. Broad adoption is also complex, requiring significant organizational change across departments and systems.

Secondly, software evolves on a spectrum from "institutionalized" (e.g., SAP for standardized tasks) to "improvised" (e.g., Excel for unique cases). When improvised solutions become critical and frequent, they are eventually institutionalized, leading to new dedicated applications. AI will enhance capabilities across this entire spectrum, making free-form tools more powerful and fostering new vertical apps, but it won't eliminate this continuous cycle of bundling and unbundling.

Current enterprise AI deployments, like giving everyone Copilot, show limited widespread impact, akin to early PC or internet adoption. True transformation requires companies to address three strategic questions: how to deploy the technology, how it alters operations, and its impact on business economics and competitive landscape. These complex challenges will drive demand for professional services. Ultimately, while AI will accelerate existing workflows, its most significant impact will arise from enabling entirely new, previously unimaginable possibilities.
chinese_title: 人工智能、工具与转型
chinese_summary:
文章《人工智能、工具与转型》挑战了人工智能将毫不费力地自动化企业任务并简化软件开发的乐观观点。文章指出，尽管企业拥有庞大的软件资产，却仍旧被重复性工作所困扰。尽管人工智能承诺无需编码即可轻松创建工具，但作者认为这忽略了一些基本现实。

首先，大多数人并非“工具构建者”，也没有能力本能地识别自动化机会。核心困难不在于构建工具，而在于知道*什么*问题需要工具，以及该工具*应该*完成什么。广泛应用也十分复杂，需要跨部门和系统的重大组织变革。

其次，软件在一个“制度化”（例如，用于标准化任务的SAP）到“即兴化”（例如，用于独特情况的Excel）的范围内演进。当即兴解决方案变得关键且频繁时，它们最终会被制度化，从而催生新的专用应用程序。人工智能将增强这一整个范围内的能力，使自由形式工具更强大，并促进新的垂直应用发展，但它不会消除这种持续的捆绑和解绑循环。

当前的企业人工智能部署，例如为每个人配备Copilot，其广泛影响有限，类似于早期PC或互联网的普及。真正的转型要求企业解决三个战略问题：如何部署这项技术、它如何改变运营，以及它对商业经济和竞争格局的影响。这些复杂的挑战将推动对专业服务的需求。最终，尽管人工智能将加速现有工作流程，但其最重要的影响将源于它能够实现全新的、以前无法想象的可能性。

title: I changed my license
summary:
The author reflects on 28 years of software licensing, detailing three distinct phases. Initially, their Midgard web framework used LGPLv2, a weak copyleft license. Around 2011, for JavaScript projects, they adopted the permissive MIT license, popular in the NPM ecosystem for its simplicity.

After a period of inactivity, the author has now made the European Union Public License 1.2 (EUPL-1.2) their default. This marks a significant pivot to a strong copyleft license. The author explains this change as a disillusionment with permissive licenses, arguing that the "open source" movement inadvertently benefited corporations and billionaires rather than users or developers. EUPL-1.2 aims to rectify this by closing the "SaaS loophole," mandating reciprocal licensing regardless of how the software is distributed. The author believes corporations unwilling to adhere to these terms should develop their own solutions. An additional benefit of EUPL-1.2 is its 23 official translations, facilitating global use.

Several new projects, including `reticulum-js`, `dacar`, `signalk-energy-predictor`, `offshore-blogging-system`, and the rewritten NoFlo Development Environment, are now under EUPL-1.2. However, the pre-existing NoFlo project will remain MIT-licensed due to its history and third-party contributions.

title: Watch Los Angeles get built, one building at a time (1880–2026)
summary:
This article describes an interactive visualization project titled "Parcelscope Los Angeles," which aims to let users "watch Los Angeles get built, one building at a time" from 1880 to 2026. The project maps every building currently standing in Los Angeles, representing each with a box that appears in the year it was constructed.

Crucially, this visualization showcases "the surviving city," meaning it only includes buildings still present today, excluding those that have been torn down over the years. Users can explore the city's architectural evolution, with buildings displayed by their decade built and height, exaggerated for clarity when zoomed out. The interface allows for panning and tilting, and likely provides detailed information such as specific build year, footprint, and building type upon selection. The data for these outlines and heights is sourced from LARIAC 2020 and LA County Assessor rolls.
